stories.title: The Circle of Light
stories.fortuneLine: Your light does not push back the dark; it only tells the dark where you are.
stories.body:
A child was given a lantern and one instruction: the light does not show you the way. It shows the way you.

The child walked the forest path at dusk, holding the lantern high, and the trees stepped politely back from the glow.

Beyond the glow, the dark arranged itself. Eyes opened at the height of wolves, and higher.

The child learned the rule of the road quickly: whatever the light touched stayed a tree. Whatever it did not touch could be anything it liked.

So the child walked in the middle of a small, obedient world, twelve feet wide, that traveled with them like a room.

Years passed on that path. The child grew; the wick burned down.

The circle of light drew in a little each winter, the way a coat shrinks that is really a body growing old.

At the end it lit only a hand, then only a knuckle, then only the memory of a flame that the dark, out of an old courtesy, went on stepping back from.

The eyes never came closer. That was the mercy.

They only waited, patient as an unlit house, for the door to finish closing.
